 PS6 LIVE: Next-gen PlayStation plans official update from Sony
 Jake Brigstock An official product image of the Sony logo on a PS5 console
 Sony Interactive Entertainment
 There's been an official update on development of the next generation of PlayStation hardware, expected to be the PS6 , from a boss at Sony .
 Tech specs, along with info about the speculated PS6 handheld console understood to be called Project Canis, have also been previously 'leaked' by a renowned tech insider.
 A former PlayStation boss thinks next-gen PlayStation console development efforts should be made on making the PS6 more affordable.
 Follow Indy100 's PS6 live blog below for all the latest Sony announcements, release date, price developments, hardware news, specs, specifications and other confirmed updates and rumours about the next-generation PlayStation.
 PS6 plans official update from Sony
 Sony shared an earnings update for the most recent financial quarter and CFO Lin Tao spoke about development of the next generation of PlayStation.
 Speaking in an earnings call (via Video Games Chronicle ), she said looking ahead to the next fiscal year, "we intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-gen platform" and that "solid progress" is already being made in terms of development.
 "From next fiscal year onward, there will be investment in the new platform," she added. 
 "For future growth, we have to attach great importance to a new platform and make the necessary investments for that.
 "We have to support the soundness of our platform and think about how rationally we can invest in that platform. We will announce that at an appropriate time in the future."
 GTA 6 most pre-ordered game on PlayStation Store
 It's been officially confirmed GTA 6 is the most pre-ordered game on both PlayStation and XBOX digital storefronts.
 The official PlayStation X / Twitter account confirmed this in a social media post and XBOX CEO Asha Sharma confirmed the game is the most pre-ordered through Microsoft Store.
 Cheaper PS6 console should be priority says former PlayStation boss
 Former Sony Interactive Entertainment America president and CEO Shawn Layden thinks the next-gen PlayStation should have more focus on being affordable.
 Layden said on The Trophy Room podcast : "I think we have enough power in the machine.
 "The innovation needs to come from not making PS6 $1,200, it's to make another PS5 for $300. That would be true innovation.
 "This is the first platform [PS5] that I've seen go up in price over time; at the end of the PS2 era it was $99 and that's how you accelerate the explosion of the install base."
